messages:
hannah: onboarding snag: installed redwoodctl via apt on Ubuntu (deb from our packages) and also tried snap on another machine. Both show `redwoodctl auth login` success, but my systemd user service for `redwoodctl local-serve@project.service` starts and immediately logs `rpc: unauthenticated`. Wondering if systemd unit environment differs from interactive shell and breaks token discovery.

vijay: plausible. systemd user services have a limited env (no XDG_CONFIG_HOME unless set in unit). Which backend did you use (file vs keyring)? And where did the token land?

hannah: apt-installer wrote token to /home/hannah/.redwood/token (file backend). snap-installed binary wrote to /home/hannah/.config/redwood/token (XDG). Systemd unit runs as my user but not through a login shell. Service unit file is simple: ExecStart=/usr/bin/redwoodctl local serve --project=project. No REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR exported.

kevin: that explains it: service can't see XDG env so snap install token (XDG) isn't visible. For apt case, service might be using a different HOME (if unit has DynamicUser or something) or running before postinstall wrote token. Can you paste `systemctl --user show-environment` and `systemctl --user status redwoodctl\u0000@project.service` logs?

hannah: `systemctl --user show-environment` -> no XDG vars. Status logs show startup then `rpc: unauthenticated` and then crash. I also tried `Environment=REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR=/home/hannah/.config/redwood` in the unit and service started fine.

vijay: workaround is to set Environment in unit or place token in legacy ~/.redwood path that systemd will find when HOME is correct. But we need robust defaults: CLI should look at both XDG and legacy paths and also respect systemd behavior. Could add logic: if running under systemd (detect $INVOCATION_ID or notify socket) and no XDG set, also check common paths.

kevin: we should also ensure packaging scripts don't rely on postinstall hooks that write tokens as root; that can end up with wrong ownership. For apt: did installer write token as the user or attempted per-user write via postinst?

hannah: apt package used a postinst that drops a welcome file in /etc and then invoked a helper `redwoodctl-init` which attempted an interactive auth if run in a tty; looks like on my machine the helper didn't run. So token was only created when I ran interactive login. The service was started by a user-level login manager that auto-starts systemd units; since my first interactive login happened later, the service saw no token initially.

vijay: two separate fixes: packaging - avoid attempting to write per-user tokens during install; onboarding - add a systemd unit example with Environment line; CLI - probe both XDG and legacy locations and on unauthenticated RPC attempt a silent re-check of disk/token to give friendly recovery. Also add `redwoodctl install --systemd-user` that writes a unit with correct env.

kevin: I'll open GH issue and label packaging + docs + cli: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/1207 "packaging & systemd: sample unit + config-dir parity + install-time behaviour" with repro steps. Suggestion: unit template should include `Environment=REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR=%h/.config/redwood` and a comment about `--user` services not inheriting shell env.

devex-bot: doc note: add a line to Linux quickstart about systemd `Environment` for services, and a snippet for `redwoodctl --generate-systemd` to produce a ready-to-use unit. Also add a test that starts a systemd user unit in CI (or a container simulation) to catch regressions.

hannah: added repro to the issue with apt vs snap outputs and the working unit file contents. For now I'll keep the Environment workaround in our local dotfiles. Thanks folks. :thumbsup:
